input:
Bug report:
[epistemic] β⁹ GTT week-4 step A — body-level precision via parameter-index tracking

At direct user-fn call sites, replace the week-3 union-all rule
(every argument's channel set flows into the return) with a
per-callee body-precision rule: union only those B9_ARG_CH_SET
slots whose parameter index the callee body actually references at
return position.  `fn first(a, b) = a` now types at {arg₀} rather
than {arg₀ ∪ arg₁}.

Mechanics: new EXPR_PARAM_USED expression-level bitmask paired with
EXPR_CH_SET at every propagation site (primaries, binops, atan2 /
pow, let-store, var-load), persisted through let/load via
VAR_PARAM_USED (mirror of week-2 VAR_CH_SET), seeded for parameters
at function prologue (x86 + a64), captured at body tail into
FN_USED_PARAMS[fi] with bit 62 = FN_USED_ANALYZED marking analyzed
functions.  At call sites, B9_ARG_PARAM_USED holds per-arg
enclosing-fn dependency so the call-site return carries body
precision into the caller's own enclosing-fn's EXPR_PARAM_USED.
Sentinel 0 and param indices ≥ 16 both fall back to the week-3
conservative union.

Canary: tests/run-pass/gtt_body_precision_param_usage.sio —
hessian_of(proj_a(k0.value, k1.value), 0, 0) still accepted.
Refusal: tests/compile-fail/gtt_body_precision_unused_param_refused.sio
— hessian_of(proj_a(k0.value, k1.value), 1, 1) now refused at

Bug report:
[compiler] β² fix: expression-hash dispatch covers all three blindness cases

Extends the direct-source β fix (3dc8b595) with expression-hash tracking
so the dispatch unifies v1, v2, v3 from variance_covariance_blindness:

  v1  Var(x - x)           0.000 (was 0.02)   [already by β]
  v2  Var(a·b - a·b)       0.000 (was 0.065)  [new by β²]
  v3  Var((x+1) - (x+1))   0.000 (was 0.02)   [new by β²]

Mechanism. Each uncertain expression in the compiler now carries a
compile-time EXPR_VARIANCE_HASH that represents its variance derivation:
- measure()/.value seeds hash = slot*2 + 1 (non-zero, slot-specific)
- arithmetic ops combine left/right hashes with the op code, producing a
  unique hash per distinct derivation tree
- let-bindings persist the hash to VAR_VARIANCE_HASH[slot] alongside the
  variance copy
- variable loads restore EXPR_VARIANCE_HASH from the variable's stored
  hash

Binop dispatch in compile_additive and compile_multiplicative now checks
`left_vhash != 0 && left_vhash == right_vhash` — if so, the two operands
are known to have identical variance values (same expression, possibly
via different SSA slots or let-bindings). Same-variant emit fires; the
existing emit_variance_addsub_same_x86 (for real slots) and the Part B
emit_variance_addsub_same_scratch_x86 (for scratch) are sufficient — no
new emit functions needed.

Correctness note. Two let-bindings from the same RHS expression can
alias to a shared hash. The variance values in their BSS slots are
actually equal (same input, same deterministic computation at emit-
time), so picking either slot's variance for the same-variant emit is
safe. This is not true if RHS involves impure function calls — but
Sounio functions returning Knowledge<f64> are rare and their .value
access is what gets hashed, not the function itself, keeping the
equivalence sound for supported patterns.

gen1/gen2/gen3.

  v2  Var(a·b - a·b)       0.000 (was 0.065)  [new by β²]
  v3  Var((x+1) - (x+1))   0.000 (was 0.02)   [new by β²]

Mechanism. Each uncertain expression in the compiler now carries a
compile-time EXPR_VARIANCE_HASH that represents its variance derivation:
- measure()/.value seeds hash = slot*2 + 1 (non-zero, slot-specific)
- arithmetic ops combine left/right hashes with the op code, producing a
  unique hash per distinct derivation tree
- let-bindings persist the hash to VAR_VARIANCE_HASH[slot] alongside the
  variance copy
- variable loads restore EXPR_VARIANCE_HASH from the variable's stored
  hash

Binop dispatch in compile_additive and compile_multiplicative now checks
`left_vhash != 0 && left_vhash == right_vhash` — if so, the two operands
are known to have identical variance values (same expression, possibly
via different SSA slots or let-bindings). Same-variant emit fires; the
existing emit_variance_addsub_same_x86 (for real slots) and the Part B
emit_variance_addsub_same_scratch_x86 (for scratch) are sufficient — no
new emit functions needed.

Correctness note. Two let-bindings from the same RHS expression can
alias to a shared hash. The variance values in their BSS slots are
actually equal (same input, same deterministic computation at emit-
time), so picking either slot's variance for the same-variant emit is
safe. This is not true if RHS involves impure function calls — but
Sounio functions returning Knowledge<f64> are rare and their .value
access is what gets hashed, not the function itself, keeping the
equivalence sound for supported patterns.

Bootstrap fixed-point: md5 f89cadc8948a7c1d5eb183198d9ada66 across
gen1/gen2/gen3.

Regression. rapamycin_iso_budget, gum_iso_budget, rapamycin_rk4_budget
all IDENTICAL to baseline. gum_iso_budget_ode numerically narrower
(var_total 4.095 → 4.000) — the Euler step `y + h·k·y` previously
double-counted the y-uncertainty across the two y-references on the
RHS; β² correctly collapses it. Test still PASSES. All other variance-
using tests (shadow, octonion-structure, gum_vs_mc, MC) PASS.

Follow-up (not in scope): function-call purity annotation so that
`f() - f()` can also use hash dispatch when `f` is pure. Currently
function-call return variance gets hash 0 (not tracked), so it falls
through to gate dispatch — conservative but correct.

Bug report:
[epistemic] Track B: R15 runtime tag stack — --r15-monitor flag

Implement the R15 confidence monitor (Track B). When compiled with
--r15-monitor, the Sounio compiler instruments every call site with:

  cmp  qword [r15 + gate_id*8], 950   ; side-table lookup
  jge  .ok                            ; skip if confident
  ud2                                 ; SIGILL trap
  .ok:

R15 is loaded at _start with the absolute address of a BSS side table
(one i64 per call site). The trampoline initialises all entries to 1000
via a tight loop before calling main.

Implementation details:
- CLI_R15_MONITOR global + --r15-monitor flag parser
- R15_SIDE_TABLE_BSS_OFF: BSS allocation (16384*8 = 131KB reserved)
- R15_GATE_COUNT: sequential gate ID counter per compilation
- Gate emission: CMP/JGE/UD2 using optimal ModRM encoding
  (mod=00 for gate_id=0, mod=01 for disp≤127, mod=10 otherwise)
- Linux trampoline: mov r15, abs64 + fill-loop + then call main
- Stats: "r15_monitor: N sites instrumented, side_table_size=M bytes"

Bug report:
[compiler] add pub const support to lean_single.sio (x86 path)

Implement compile-time constant resolution for `pub const NAME: TYPE = VALUE`
declarations. Three-phase approach:

1. scan_all_consts(): pre-pass scans all tokens for `pub const` declarations,
   populates CONST_NS/CONST_NE/CONST_VAL/CONST_COUNT tables (512 entries each)
2. const_find_val(): looks up a name in the constant table, stores the value
   in CONST_FOUND_VAL global, returns 1 if found / 0 if not

   emits `xor rax, rax` (zero) or `mov rax, imm64` (non-zero) for the constant

overflows its 128-slot limit, corrupting let-binding slot tracking. Direct
reads of globals (CONST_FOUND_VAL, CONST_COUNT etc.) work correctly; only
`let cv = GLOBAL` is broken. Fix: eliminate the intermediate let binding
and reference CONST_FOUND_VAL directly in the conditional check.

Bug report:
[native,lexer] Sprint 234 Track A: closure gate PASS — lean emitter exits 6

ExprClosure lambda-lifting in lean emitter now produces correct ELF.
|x: i64| x + 1 applied to 5 exits 6 (verified).

Fixes:
- fn_offsets[fn_idx] moved AFTER ast_compile_fn_body so closure flush
  (which advances WIDE_LEN during body compilation) doesn't corrupt the
  enclosing function's start offset
- MAIN_FN_IDX promoted to global (var) to survive JIT register-clobber
  heisenbug: ir_empty_name() SRET calls corrupt caller-saved regs holding
  local main_fn_idx across the builtin registration block
- prog_items_prefetch: force-read prog.items after load_source_file to
  materialize the SRET Program before Phase 0/1 accesses it; without this
  read the JIT reuses the SRET buffer causing prog.items to appear None
- Early MAIN_FN_IDX < 0 check before ir_empty_name() builtin loop
- Lexer LexerState::new: copy source → CURSOR_SOURCE inline so boot4
  cursor reads real file data (boot4 passes BSS addr for local arrays)
- CL_BODY_NAMES/SLOTS/COUNT globals ([Name;8]) for closure param scope;
  ast_compile_closure_body_expr avoids [Name;512] JIT IR explosion
- Closure LEA post-pass: sentinel 48 8D 05 <cidx_lo> <cidx_hi> C1 BE
  patched to real RIP-relative displacement after all fns flushed

and linear resource tracking in a single closure type constructor:

- All FnSig literals updated (4 sites in check.sio + empty_fn_sig)

- check_closure_expr scans outer-scope bindings for linear + epistemic types
- Conservative: all visible outer bindings checked (sound over-approximation)
- Linear captures: set is_linear_closure = true
- Epistemic captures: combine epsilons, auto-add Epistemic effect (ID 8)

uncertainty metadata, and linearity constraints in a unified type.

[stdlib] Sprint 228: first-class functions — fn refs, closures, higher-order ops

IR layer:

- ExprCall: indirect dispatch when callee is a local variable

Native codegen (lower_ir.sio):

fn _emit_legal_byval(func: MachineFunction, instr: MachineInstr) -> MachineFunction with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var f = func
    if f.blocks[0].instr_count < 512 {
        f.blocks[0].instrs[f.blocks[0].instr_count as usize] = instr
        f.blocks[0].instr_count = f.blocks[0].instr_count + 1
        f.legal_instr_count = f.legal_instr_count + 1
    }
    f
}

        f.blocks[0].instrs[f.blocks[0].instr_count as usize] = instr
        f.blocks[0].instr_count = f.blocks[0].instr_count + 1
    }
    f

fn _emit_legal_byval(func: MachineFunction, instr: MachineInstr) -> MachineFunction with Mut, Panic, Div {
    var f = func
    if f.blocks[0].instr_count < 512 {
        f.blocks[0].instrs[f.blocks[0].instr_count as usize] = instr
        f.blocks[0].instr_count = f.blocks[0].instr_count + 1
        f.legal_instr_count = f.legal_instr_count + 1
    }
    f
}

    f

[ir,compiler] Sprint 88: fix E017 deref-index in find_or_add_fn_id

Both find_or_add_fn_id (method) and lowerer_find_or_add_fn_id_mut (free fn)
had 7 consecutive (*lo.module).functions[idx as usize] field assignments —
triggering the JIT E017 bug (second+ (*ref)[idx] in same function body
dispatches to check_call_expr instead of check_index_expr).

Fix: use ir_empty_function() to initialise a local IrFunction value, set
.name, then assign the whole value with a single (*lo.module).functions[idx] =
new_fn expression. Reduces deref-index occurrences from 7 → 1 in both sites.

examples/render/triangle_basic.sio now reaches the full lowering pass
without crashing on the first fn item (vertex).

Bug report:
[backend] fix CPUID gate in emit_avx10_detect for legacy AVX-512F path

SOBC VM emits wrong byte for SETNE (0x94 vs 0x95) at this specific
call site due to a VM byte-emission bug. Replace the SETNE/MOVZX/SHL
sequence with a branch-based approach: XOR r15d,r15d then JZ .done then
MOV r15d,4. Also fix r15d register encoding (was 41 BD = r13d, now
41 BF = r15d). Legacy block shrinks 27 → 26 bytes; JMP offset updated.

Verified: float_arith.sio exit=0, mutvar.sio exit=0 on AVX-512F host.

Old code:
// JMP .done  (EB 1B, rel8 = 27: skip 27-byte .no_avx10 block)
    b = emit_byte(b, 0xEB); b = emit_byte(b, 27)
    // SETNE al  (0F 95 C0): al = 1 if AVX-512F present (ZF=0 means bit was set)
    b = emit_byte(b, 0x0F); b = emit_byte(b, 0x95); b = emit_byte(b, 0xC0)
    // MOVZX eax, al  (0F B6 C0): zero-extend, eax = 0 or 1
    b = emit_byte(b, 0x0F); b = emit_byte(b, 0xB6); b = emit_byte(b, 0xC0)
    // SHL eax, 2  (C1 E0 02): 1 → 4 (bit2 = 512-bit in VL mask convention)
    b = emit_byte(b, 0xC1); b = emit_byte(b, 0xE0); b = emit_byte(b, 2)
    // MOV r15d, eax  (41 89 C7): store VL mask in r15
    b = emit_byte(b, 0x41); b = emit_byte(b, 0x89); b = emit_byte(b, 0xC7)
